fix_title: Verify the auxiliary output's parameter assignment with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a dealer-level diagnostic tool and read the auxiliary output configuration • 2. Confirm it matches the solenoid actually wired on the truck • 3. Correct the parameter and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the assigned solenoid valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air line and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the diff lock, transfer case, trailer or 3/2 valve solenoid • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and function-test

fix_title: Identify the assigned solenoid and inspect its connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Use the diagnostic tool to read which function (diff lock, transfer case, trailer, 3/2 valve) the output is configured for • 2. Locate and inspect that solenoid's connector for corrosion • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the auxiliary output driver circuit for a short or open
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the output pin at the ECU and measure resistance to the solenoid coil • 2. Check for a short to ground or voltage along the harness • 3. Repair the wiring and re-test

fix_title: Read and clear codes, then cycle ignition and re-scan for a repeat fault
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Record all active and stored codes • 2. Clear codes and cycle ignition off/on • 3. Re-scan and road-test to see if the fault re-sets

fix_title: Update the ECU software to the latest calibration
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the dealer diagnostic tool and check the current software level • 2. Apply the latest released calibration/update • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Replace the ABS/ESC ECU
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the internal fault repeats after a software update and power-supply check • 2. Replace the ECU with the correct part number for the vehicle configuration • 3. Complete dealer end-of-line programming and configuration

fix_title: Verify the connection between the main ECU and any add-on ESC/safety module
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Inspect the harness/connector linking the main ABS ECU and the ESC module • 2. Check for corrosion, an open pin, or a loose connector • 3. Repair and clear codes

fix_title: Verify wheel-speed sensor wiring matches the correct wheel position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm each sensor connector is routed to its labeled ECU pin • 2. Correct any swapped or reversed left/right connections • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Replace a worn or damaged tone ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Access and remove the damaged tone ring • 2. Press on the replacement ring • 3. Reassemble, set the air gap and road-test

fix_title: Clean the tone ring and check sensor mounting security
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove debris and metal fines from the tone ring teeth • 2. Confirm the sensor is fully seated and not vibrating loose • 3. Clear codes and road-test through a speed range

fix_title: Replace a mismatched tire so the axle set matches
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the tire(s) that do not match the axle set • 2. Replace with a correctly sized/matched tire • 3. Re-verify sizes and pressures, then clear codes

fix_title: Verify matched tire sizes and pressures across the axle
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure rolling circumference or check size/load ratings on each tire of the axle • 2. Correct pressure to spec on all positions • 3. Note any mismatched tire for replacement

fix_title: Replace a worn or damaged tone ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Access and remove the damaged tone ring • 2. Press on the replacement ring • 3. Reassemble, set the air gap and road-test

fix_title: Clean the tone ring and check sensor mounting security
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove debris and metal fines from the tone ring teeth • 2. Confirm the sensor is fully seated and not vibrating loose • 3. Clear codes and road-test through a speed range

fix_title: Replace a mismatched tire so the axle set matches
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the tire(s) that do not match the axle set • 2. Replace with a correctly sized/matched tire • 3. Re-verify sizes and pressures, then clear codes

fix_title: Verify wheel-speed sensor wiring matches the correct wheel position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm each sensor connector is routed to its labeled ECU pin • 2. Correct any swapped or reversed left/right connections • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Verify matched tire sizes and pressures across the axle
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure rolling circumference or check size/load ratings on each tire of the axle • 2. Correct pressure to spec on all positions • 3. Note any mismatched tire for replacement

fix_title: Inspect and clean the modulator valve connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the valve connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Clean, apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the hold/release solenoid coil resistance and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the hold and release coil pins and measure resistance against spec • 2. Check for a short to ground or to voltage on the harness • 3. Repair or replace the wiring as needed

fix_title: Replace the ABS pressure modulator valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air lines and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the modulator valve, torquing fittings per spec • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Check the modulator for a sticking spool or internal air leak
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Listen and feel for continuous air flow or chatter at the valve • 2. Cycle the valve with a diagnostic tool and observe exhaust/response • 3. Replace the valve if it sticks or leaks internally

fix_title: Inspect and clean the modulator valve connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the valve connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Clean, apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the hold/release solenoid coil resistance and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the hold and release coil pins and measure resistance against spec • 2. Check for a short to ground or to voltage on the harness • 3. Repair or replace the wiring as needed

fix_title: Replace the ABS pressure modulator valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air lines and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the modulator valve, torquing fittings per spec • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Check the modulator for a sticking spool or internal air leak
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Listen and feel for continuous air flow or chatter at the valve • 2. Cycle the valve with a diagnostic tool and observe exhaust/response • 3. Replace the valve if it sticks or leaks internally

fix_title: Run the steering angle sensor calibration procedure with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Center the steering wheel, wheels straight, vehicle on level ground • 2. Run the SAS calibration in the diagnostic tool • 3. Verify the learned zero point and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the steering angle sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the steering column trim and disconnect the sensor • 2. Install the replacement sensor • 3. Reassemble and run the calibration procedure

fix_title: Inspect and reseat the steering angle sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the SAS connector under the steering column • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Verify the SAS is correctly centered and securely mounted on the column
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check the sensor housing for secure mounting and correct orientation • 2. Confirm the steering wheel is centered with the wheels straight ahead • 3. Re-seat or re-align as needed

fix_title: Verify the underlying system condition the sensor is reporting
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm whether the out-of-range reading reflects a real system fault or a bad sensor • 2. Inspect the related system for the root physical cause • 3. Repair as needed, then clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Replace the fuel temperature sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor's live reading against a known-good reference (scan tool or hand-held meter) • 2. Remove and replace the sensor, torque per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify the new reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel temperature sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the fuel temperature sensor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the accelerator pedal position sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or oil/coolant intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the accelerator pedal position sensor signal and supply circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe signal, ground and supply-voltage pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts and correct reference voltage • 3. Repair chafed wiring or corroded splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the accelerator pedal position sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify sensor air-gap or mounting per OEM spec • 2. Remove and replace the sensor and O-ring/seal • 3. Set the correct gap or torque, clear codes and verify signal quality on a scan tool

fix_title: Check the sensed target (gear teeth, reluctor ring, linkage) for damage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Inspect the reluctor wheel, gear teeth or mechanical linkage the sensor reads for damage, debris or wear • 2. Repair or replace the damaged component • 3. Reinstall the sensor, clear codes and verify

fix_title: Inspect and clean the engine coolant temperature sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat the connector, clear codes and recheck live data

fix_title: Test the engine coolant temperature sensor signal, ground and reference circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal, ground and 5V/8V reference pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and resistance in range • 3. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, reseal splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the engine coolant temperature sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor's live reading against a known-good reference (scan tool or hand-held meter) • 2. Remove and replace the sensor, torque per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify the new reading tracks correctly

fix_title: Verify the underlying system condition the sensor is reporting
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm whether the out-of-range reading reflects a real system fault or a bad sensor • 2. Inspect the related system for the root physical cause • 3. Repair as needed, then clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Check ECU power, ground and case-connector integrity
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect the main ECU harness connectors for corrosion, bent pins or moisture intrusion • 2. Check the ECU's power and ground straps for a clean, tight connection • 3. Reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test ECU supply and ground circuit wiring for the affected channel
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify battery voltage reaches the ECU's power pins with the key on • 2. Check chassis ground points for corrosion or a poor connection • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the engine control unit (ECU) (or the affected internal module)
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault persists after a reflash and clean power/ground • 2. Replace the ECU/module and transfer or re-program its configuration data • 3. Clear codes and verify with a full system scan

fix_title: Reflash/reprogram the engine control unit (ECU) with the latest calibration
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM diagnostic tool and check for a newer software/calibration release • 2. Reflash the ECU per the OEM procedure • 3. Clear codes, run a full DTC scan and road-test

fix_title: Test the fuel injector driver circuit resistance and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil/solenoid resistance at the connector against OEM spec • 2. Check the harness back to the ECU/injector driver for opens or shorts • 3. Repair or replace the harness section as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the fuel injector connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the injector connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, heat damage or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the fuel injector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm which cylinder/position is faulted from live data or cylinder cutout test • 2. Remove and replace the injector, use new seals/washers per OEM spec • 3. Torque to spec, prime the fuel system, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Perform injector trim/coding reset after service
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Enter the injector serial/trim code from the new injector into the ECU (or reset adaptive trims) using the OEM diagnostic tool • 2. Clear codes • 3. Verify smooth idle and no misfire/imbalance codes return

fix_title: Free and clean the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the valve and inspect for sticking, varnish or debris • 2. Clean and free the moving element, or replace if seized • 3. Reinstall, clear codes and verify

fix_title: Check the related system pressure and condition
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify the system pressure the valve regulates is within spec with a gauge • 2. Address any upstream cause (restriction, pump wear, contamination) • 3. Clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Replace the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the valve/assembly • 2. Fit the replacement with new seals per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify correct operation

fix_title: Free and clean the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the valve and inspect for sticking, varnish or debris • 2. Clean and free the moving element, or replace if seized • 3. Reinstall, clear codes and verify

fix_title: Check the related system pressure and condition
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify the system pressure the valve regulates is within spec with a gauge • 2. Address any upstream cause (restriction, pump wear, contamination) • 3. Clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Replace the cylinder misfire/power-balance monitor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the valve/assembly • 2. Fit the replacement with new seals per OEM spec • 3. Clear codes and verify correct operation

fix_title: Test the LCA position sensor and drive circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the LCA signal, return and drive circuits at the TECU connector • 2. Check for the reference voltage and continuity to the actuator • 3. Repair chafed or open conductors and reseal any splices

fix_title: Inspect and clean the LCA wiring connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the LCA connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, spread terminals and moisture intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect, clear codes and cycle the clutch

fix_title: Replace the Linear Clutch Actuator (LCA) assembly
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Support the transmission and disconnect the air supply to the actuator • 2. Remove the LCA assembly and transfer or replace the mounting hardware • 3. Fit the new LCA, reconnect wiring and air lines, then run the clutch touch-point learn

fix_title: Relearn the clutch touch-point with ServiceRanger
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and select the clutch calibration routine • 2. Follow the guided touch-point learn sequence with the engine at operating temperature • 3. Verify the learned values fall within Eaton's expected range and clear codes

fix_title: Inspect the clutch linkage, release bearing and pressure plate
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the inspection cover and check linkage travel and free play • 2. Inspect the release bearing and pressure plate fingers for wear or damage • 3. Adjust or repair as needed and re-verify LCA travel

fix_title: Verify supply air is at or above 100 psi and check the air dryer/regulator/lines
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check gauge pressure at the TECU air pack with the engine running and air system charged • 2. Inspect the air dryer, governor and supply lines for restriction, leaks or moisture • 3. Repair the air system and re-verify pressure at the pack

fix_title: Replace the air supply pressure sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Isolate and bleed the air supply line to the sensor • 2. Remove and replace the sensor • 3. Restore air supply, leak-check the fitting, clear codes and verify live pressure data

fix_title: Inspect and clean the air supply pressure sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the sensor signal circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal and return pins at the TECU connector • 2. Check for reference voltage and continuity to the sensor • 3. Repair chafed or open conductors

fix_title: Check fluid level/condition, filter and lube pump for a genuine low-pressure condition
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check fluid level and condition with the vehicle level and at operating temperature • 2. Inspect and replace the transmission filter if restricted • 3. If pressure remains low with a known-good sensor, inspect the lube pump and pickup screen

fix_title: Replace the transmission oil pressure sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Drain fluid below the sensor location if required • 2. Remove and replace the sensor with the correct thread sealant • 3. Refill, clear codes and verify live pressure data

fix_title: Recalibrate the pressure sensor scaling with ServiceRanger
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and compare the live reading to a shop pressure gauge at the test port • 2. Run the sensor scaling/calibration routine if available • 3. Clear codes and re-verify

fix_title: Inspect and clean the oil pressure sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the pressure sensor signal circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal and return pins at the TECU connector • 2. Check for reference voltage and continuity to the sensor • 3. Repair chafed or open conductors

fix_title: Replace the countershaft speed sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the sensor from its bore • 2. Fit the new sensor, setting the air gap or torque per the Eaton service manual • 3. Reconnect, clear codes and verify live speed data

fix_title: Check the sensor air gap and tone ring/gear for damage or debris
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the sensor and inspect the tip for metal debris or damage • 2. Inspect the tone ring/gear teeth for wear or damage • 3. Clean debris, reset the air gap and reinstall

fix_title: Inspect and clean the countershaft speed sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the countershaft speed sensor signal circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal and return pins at the TECU connector • 2. Check for chafed or open conductors between the sensor and the TECU • 3. Repair or reseal as needed

fix_title: Test the sensor signal and return circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal and return pins at the TECU connector • 2. Check for the reference voltage and resistance to ground • 3. Repair chafed or open conductors

fix_title: Inspect and clean the oil temperature sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor • 2. Check pins for corrosion, spread terminals and fluid intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the transmission oil temperature sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Drain fluid below the sensor location • 2. Remove the sensor and fit the new one with sealant per Eaton spec • 3. Refill, clear codes and verify live data against an infrared reading

fix_title: Diagnose a genuine overheating condition (fluid level, cooler, duty cycle)
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the reading with an infrared thermometer at the pan or housing • 2. Check fluid level/condition and cooler airflow or coolant flow • 3. Repair the cause, then clear and re-check under load

fix_title: Replace the output shaft speed sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the sensor from its bore • 2. Fit the new sensor, setting the air gap or torque per the Eaton service manual • 3. Reconnect, clear codes and verify live speed data

fix_title: Check the sensor air gap and tone ring/gear for damage or debris
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the sensor and inspect the tip for metal debris or damage • 2. Inspect the tone ring/gear teeth for wear or damage • 3. Clean debris, reset the air gap and reinstall

fix_title: Inspect and clean the output shaft speed sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the output shaft speed sensor signal circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal and return pins at the TECU connector • 2. Check for chafed or open conductors between the sensor and the TECU • 3. Repair or reseal as needed

fix_title: Replace the LCA or position sensor if confirmation never matches actuator position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the discrepancy is not mechanical (previous fix) • 2. Replace the Linear Clutch Actuator assembly • 3. Run the clutch touch-point learn and re-verify engagement confirmation

fix_title: Inspect the clutch disc, pressure plate and release mechanism for slippage or wear
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the inspection cover • 2. Check disc lining thickness, pressure plate finger travel and the release bearing • 3. Repair or replace worn components and re-verify engagement

fix_title: Update the TECU calibration/software to the current Eaton release
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and check the installed calibration level against Eaton's current release • 2. Apply the update if available • 3. Clear codes and re-verify engagement logic

fix_title: Verify actual clutch engagement with a road test and live data
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and monitor LCA position, engine speed and input shaft speed together • 2. Drive through launch and shift events • 3. Confirm whether the engagement state matches the commanded state or lags/never matches

fix_title: Run the grade sensor calibration/relearn with ServiceRanger
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Park the vehicle on a known-level surface • 2. Connect ServiceRanger and run the grade sensor calibration/relearn routine • 3. Verify the learned zero-point and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the grade/inclination sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the sensor from its mount • 2. Fit the replacement sensor at the correct orientation • 3. Reconnect, clear codes and verify live data on level ground

fix_title: Inspect and clean the grade sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the grade sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the grade sensor signal circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the signal and return pins at the TECU connector • 2. Check for reference voltage and continuity to the sensor • 3. Repair chafed or open conductors

fix_title: Verify grade sensor mounting and orientation
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the sensor is mounted at the chassis location and orientation the OEM specifies • 2. Check for a loose, shifted or incorrectly oriented mount that would skew the reading • 3. Re-torque or re-orient the sensor and re-check the reading against a level reference

fix_title: Verify the grade sensor value is arriving on the J1939 bus without a flagged error
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger or a bus analyzer and confirm the grade/inclination message is present and not flagged invalid • 2. Check the sending module's own status and the network wiring/termination if the value is flagged invalid • 3. Only replace the sensor if the network path checks out but the value remains implausible

fix_title: Verify the TECU is receiving valid J1939 network traffic before treating this as an internal fault
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger or a bus analyzer and confirm J1939 traffic is present with no bus-off condition • 2. Check for other active network faults (see the network group) that could explain the update-rate/network-error reading • 3. Only proceed to a software update or TECU replacement once the network itself checks out

fix_title: Update the TECU software/calibration to the current Eaton release
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and check the installed software/calibration level • 2. Apply Eaton's current release if available • 3. Clear codes and monitor for recurrence

fix_title: Replace the TECU if the internal fault persists after a software update
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm power, ground, network and software have all been ruled out • 2. Replace the TECU and transfer the vehicle configuration with ServiceRanger • 3. Run the required calibrations and clear codes

fix_title: Verify TECU power, ground and network wiring are within spec
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check TECU battery/ignition supply voltage per the TECU power supply family • 2. Check J1939 network wiring per the network group's diagnosis • 3. Repair any fault found before proceeding

fix_title: Cycle key power and confirm the fault does not immediately return
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Clear codes with ServiceRanger • 2. Cycle the ignition key off and on • 3. Recheck for the active fault before further diagnosis

fix_title: Cycle key power and confirm the fault does not immediately return
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Clear codes with ServiceRanger • 2. Cycle the ignition key off and on • 3. Recheck for the active fault before further diagnosis

fix_title: Replace the TECU if the internal fault persists after a software update
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm power, ground, network and software have all been ruled out • 2. Replace the TECU and transfer the vehicle configuration with ServiceRanger • 3. Run the required calibrations and clear codes

fix_title: Verify TECU power, ground and network wiring are within spec
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check TECU battery/ignition supply voltage per the TECU power supply family • 2. Check J1939 network wiring per the network group's diagnosis • 3. Repair any fault found before proceeding

fix_title: Update the TECU software/calibration to the current Eaton release
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and check the installed software/calibration level • 2. Apply Eaton's current release if available • 3. Clear codes and monitor for recurrence

fix_title: Verify the TECU is receiving valid J1939 network traffic before treating this as an internal fault
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger or a bus analyzer and confirm J1939 traffic is present with no bus-off condition • 2. Check for other active network faults (see the network group) that could explain the update-rate/network-error reading • 3. Only proceed to a software update or TECU replacement once the network itself checks out

fix_title: Inspect and clean the shift selector connector and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the shift selector connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the shift selector signal circuit and its network wiring for opens/shorts
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the selector signal circuit at the TECU connector • 2. On a multiplexed selector, check the CAN/PWM wiring pair for proper termination and continuity • 3. Repair chafed or open conductors

fix_title: Replace the shift lever, shift pad or selector module
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the console/dash trim to access the selector • 2. Disconnect and replace the shift lever, pad or selector module • 3. Reinstall, clear codes and verify shift requests in ServiceRanger live data

fix_title: Update the TECU software and verify the configured selector type
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and check the configured shift-device type against the installed hardware • 2. Correct the configuration if mismatched • 3. Update TECU software if a related bulletin exists, then clear codes

fix_title: Verify the shift device message or PWM signal is present and updating at the expected rate
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger (or a bus analyzer for the J1939 primary shift device) and confirm the shift request message or PWM signal is present and updating • 2. Check the J1939/PWM wiring, termination and the sending module's own status before assuming the selector itself is at fault • 3. Only replace the shift lever, pad or selector module if the link checks out but the request is still missing or invalid

fix_title: Check supply air pressure and inspect the rail for mechanical binding
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify supply air is at or above 100 psi at the shifter air pack • 2. Cycle the rail by hand (transmission in neutral, air removed) and check for binding or debris • 3. Clean or repair as needed

fix_title: Replace the faulty X-Y shift rail solenoid or shifter module
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect air lines and wiring from the shifter/solenoid assembly • 2. Remove and replace the faulty solenoid or the full XY shifter module • 3. Reconnect, leak-check fittings, clear codes and run the rail calibration

fix_title: Inspect and clean the rail solenoid connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the rail solenoid connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the rail solenoid coil and drive circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil resistance against spec with the connector disconnected • 2. Back-probe the drive circuit for opens or shorts to power/ground • 3. Repair chafed wiring or a failed TECU driver

fix_title: Replace the inertia brake solenoid
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air line and wiring • 2. Remove and replace the solenoid • 3. Reconnect, leak-check the fitting and clear codes

fix_title: Run the inertia brake relearn procedure with ServiceRanger
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect ServiceRanger and select the inertia brake calibration routine • 2. Follow the guided sequence with the engine running • 3. Verify learned values are within spec and clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the inertia brake solenoid connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, disconnect the solenoid connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the solenoid coil and drive circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure coil resistance against spec with the connector disconnected • 2. Back-probe the drive circuit for opens or shorts • 3. Repair chafed wiring or a failed TECU driver

fix_title: Reconfigure the receiving controller's expected-source parameters
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM service tool to the receiving controller • 2. Check its expected-source and parameter configuration against the OEM specification for this chassis • 3. Reprogram or update as needed, clear codes, and confirm the value now arrives at the expected rate

fix_title: Scan for duplicate or unclaimed source addresses
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a J1939 scan tool at the diagnostic connector • 2. List all active source addresses and compare against the vehicle's expected device list • 3. Identify any address claimed by more than one node, or the expected controlling device's address missing entirely
procedure_rationale: This scan identifies the device involved in the conflict. A tool reading buys nothing, so no parts are listed (the scan tool formerly listed is equipment, not a repair part), and its labor is carried unchanged.

procedure_rationale: Cleans and reseats the connector of whichever device is unconfigured or in conflict. Cleaning and reseating buy nothing, so no part is needed and the old 0–20 range is not carried; the labor is carried unchanged.

fix_title: Reprogram the source address / parameter file on the affected device
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM service tool to the device with the wrong or unconfigured source address • 2. Set the correct source address per the OEM's device configuration table for this chassis • 3. Clear codes on all affected controllers and confirm no address-claim conflict remains
procedure_rationale: Uses the OEM service tool, so it is a specialist step. A reprogram changes software only, so no parts apply; any programming fee is not a parts cost (the cost basis lists it as not specified), and the labor is carried unchanged.

fix_title: Disconnect any recently added aftermarket J1939 device and recheck for the address conflict
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Review any telematics gateway, PTO controller or other aftermarket device installed since the fault began • 2. Temporarily disconnect it and recheck for the source-address conflict
procedure_rationale: Applies only when an aftermarket device was added since the fault began; disconnecting it and rechecking isolates the conflict without buying anything. The original time also covered reconfiguring the device's address, now its own procedure, so it is not carried.

fix_title: Test the 5V/8V sensor supply rail for a short or excessive load
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure the supply rail voltage at the ECU connector against OEM spec with all sensors connected, then with each disconnected in turn • 2. Isolate the shorted or overloaded branch • 3. Repair the wiring/sensor causing the short, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the regulator/relay supplying the 5V/8V sensor supply rail
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the supply is out of spec at the ECU's own output pin (points to the ECU/regulator, not the wiring) • 2. Replace the affected relay or, if internal, the ECU • 3. Clear codes and verify

fix_title: Inspect and clean the connector for this parameter's circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the connector serving this circuit (identify via the pin-out for this SPN in the OEM wiring diagram) • 2. Check pins for corrosion or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes
procedure_rationale: This step works only on the connector serving the circuit and buys no component. Its connector-kit cost and labor are carried unchanged from the original step.

fix_title: Test the circuit for an open, short or out-of-range voltage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the affected pin(s) at the module connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts to ground/battery and correct reference voltage against the OEM wiring diagram
procedure_rationale: Split from the original test-and-repair step so the circuit measurement stands as its own procedure. A measurement needs no parts, and the original time covered testing and repair together, so it is not carried.

fix_title: Replace the sensor or actuator on this circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the physical component tied to this manufacturer-specific parameter from the OEM wiring diagram or dealer tool • 2. Replace the component • 3. Clear codes and verify
procedure_rationale: Replaces the component on the affected circuit. The circuit is unidentified, so no single part applies and the old price range is not carried; the labor is carried unchanged.

fix_title: Identify the assigned solenoid and inspect its connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Use the diagnostic tool to read which function (diff lock, transfer case, trailer, 3/2 valve) the output is configured for • 2. Locate and inspect that solenoid's connector for corrosion • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Test the auxiliary output driver circuit for a short or open
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the output pin at the ECU and measure resistance to the solenoid coil • 2. Check for a short to ground or voltage along the harness • 3. Repair the wiring and re-test

fix_title: Replace the assigned solenoid valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air line and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the diff lock, transfer case, trailer or 3/2 valve solenoid • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and function-test

fix_title: Verify the auxiliary output's parameter assignment with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a dealer-level diagnostic tool and read the auxiliary output configuration • 2. Confirm it matches the solenoid actually wired on the truck • 3. Correct the parameter and clear codes

fix_title: Verify wheel-speed sensor wiring matches the correct wheel position
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm each sensor connector is routed to its labeled ECU pin • 2. Correct any swapped or reversed left/right connections • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Replace a worn or damaged tone ring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Access and remove the damaged tone ring • 2. Press on the replacement ring • 3. Reassemble, set the air gap and road-test

fix_title: Clean the tone ring and check sensor mounting security
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove debris and metal fines from the tone ring teeth • 2. Confirm the sensor is fully seated and not vibrating loose • 3. Clear codes and road-test through a speed range

fix_title: Replace a mismatched tire so the axle set matches
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Identify the tire(s) that do not match the axle set • 2. Replace with a correctly sized/matched tire • 3. Re-verify sizes and pressures, then clear codes

fix_title: Verify matched tire sizes and pressures across the axle
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Measure rolling circumference or check size/load ratings on each tire of the axle • 2. Correct pressure to spec on all positions • 3. Note any mismatched tire for replacement

fix_title: Trace and repair the sensor wiring harness
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the sensor pins at the ECU and measure coil resistance • 2. Follow the harness to the axle looking for chafe points and pinches • 3. Repair or splice the damaged run, reseal and re-test

fix_title: Inspect and clean the wheel-speed sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, moisture and spread terminals • 3. Clean, apply dielectric grease, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Replace the wheel-speed sensor

fix_title: Replace the sensor pigtail/extension harness

fix_title: Test the hold/release solenoid coil resistance and wiring
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the hold and release coil pins and measure resistance against spec • 2. Check for a short to ground or to voltage on the harness • 3. Repair or replace the wiring as needed

fix_title: Replace the ABS pressure modulator valve
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Tag and disconnect the air lines and electrical connector • 2. Remove and replace the modulator valve, torquing fittings per spec • 3. Leak-check, clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Check the modulator for a sticking spool or internal air leak
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Listen and feel for continuous air flow or chatter at the valve • 2. Cycle the valve with a diagnostic tool and observe exhaust/response • 3. Replace the valve if it sticks or leaks internally

fix_title: Verify the SAS is correctly centered and securely mounted on the column
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check the sensor housing for secure mounting and correct orientation • 2. Confirm the steering wheel is centered with the wheels straight ahead • 3. Re-seat or re-align as needed

fix_title: Replace the steering angle sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the steering column trim and disconnect the sensor • 2. Install the replacement sensor • 3. Reassemble and run the calibration procedure

fix_title: Run the steering angle sensor calibration procedure with a diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Center the steering wheel, wheels straight, vehicle on level ground • 2. Run the SAS calibration in the diagnostic tool • 3. Verify the learned zero point and clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and reseat the steering angle sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the SAS connector under the steering column • 2. Check pins for corrosion and spread terminals • 3. Clean, reconnect and clear codes

fix_title: Inspect network connectors and grounds at the diagnostic connector and main ECUs
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect the diagnostic connector and the main ECU connectors feeding the network • 2. Check for corrosion, bent pins and loose grounds • 3. Clean, reseat, clear codes and retest

step_by_step_instructions: 1. With the bus unpowered, confirm CAN H/CAN L resistance and continuity as in the physical-layer check • 2. With the bus powered, disconnect network nodes one at a time (starting with recently serviced ECUs) to find one holding the bus high, low or flooding it with traffic • 3. Repair or replace the offending node's wiring or connector

fix_title: Reconfigure the reporting ECU's multiplexing/baud parameters
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM service tool to the reporting ECU • 2. Compare its multiplexing configuration, expected source list and baud setting against the OEM specification • 3. Reprogram any parameter that does not match, then clear codes and confirm normal bus traffic

Record bus load percentage, error-frame count and the list of active source addresses • 3. Flag any address appearing twice or any node with an abnormally high error count for follow-up

fix_title: Replace the ECU if the safety-monitor fault persists after software and configuration checks
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault returns after a software update and EOL re-check • 2. Replace the ECU with the correct part number • 3. Complete dealer end-of-line programming and configuration

fix_title: Re-run end-of-line configuration if a related sensor or valve was recently replaced
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Check service history for a recent sensor, modulator or ECU replacement • 2. Re-run the EOL configuration for the affected function • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Read the full fault history and cross-reference related SPNs with a dealer scan tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Pull all active and stored codes, not just the safety-monitor SPN • 2. Cross-reference against wheel-speed, valve and sensor SPNs logged at the same time • 3. Diagnose the underlying SPN first

fix_title: Update the ECU software/calibration to the latest release
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the dealer diagnostic tool and check the current software level • 2. Apply the latest released calibration/update • 3. Clear codes and road-test

fix_title: Cycle ignition and re-scan; a transient checksum error may clear
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Record the active fault • 2. Cycle the ignition off and on • 3. Re-scan to see if the checksum fault clears

fix_title: Replace the ECU if the checksum fault returns after reprogramming
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the checksum fault repeats after a full parameter reload • 2. Replace the ECU with the correct part number • 3. Complete dealer end-of-line programming and configuration

fix_title: Re-load the vehicle configuration parameters with a dealer diagnostic tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the dealer diagnostic tool • 2. Re-enter or re-load the affected parameter group (traction control, brake, gravity/vehicle, axle configuration) • 3. Save, clear codes and road-test

step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the DEF/urea quality sensor circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the DEF/urea quality sensor heater, signal and CAN sub-network circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the heater supply, signal and network pins at the connector • 2. Check for battery voltage at the heater pin, correct signal reference and continuity/termination on the sensor's local CAN sub-network • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the DEF/urea quality sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the DEF/urea quality sensor and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the sensor at its mounting boss (exhaust pipe for NOx/O2/NH3 sensors, DEF tank for a quality sensor), torquing/sealing per spec - these are heated, CAN-networked smart sensors; aftermarket HD units commonly run $300-700 • 3. Clear codes, allow the sensor to complete its power-up self-test, and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Check DEF/urea quality sensor calibration/learned values with a service tool
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect a service tool and compare the sensor's live reading against a known reference (refractometer for DEF quality, a second sensor, or a bench check) • 2. Run the OEM's sensor learn/reset procedure if the reading is offset but the circuit tests good • 3. Clear codes and confirm the reading holds through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect, clean and reseat the DEF line heater connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the DEF line heater circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the DEF line heater circuit for opens, shorts and correct supply voltage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the circuit at the connector with the harness connected • 2. Check for supply voltage, continuity to the controller and resistance to ground/battery • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the DEF line heater
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the DEF line heater and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the component, transferring any mounting hardware • 3. Clear codes and verify normal operation through a duty cycle

fix_title: Inspect, clean and reseat the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR circuit connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals and moisture intrusion, and check the harness for chafing near hot exhaust components • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and confirm the fault does not return

fix_title: Test the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR heater, signal and CAN sub-network circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the heater supply, signal and network pins at the connector • 2. Check for battery voltage at the heater pin, correct signal reference and continuity/termination on the sensor's local CAN sub-network • 3. Repair the open, shorted or chafed conductor, reseal the splice, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault follows the NOx sensor, downstream of SCR and not the harness with a swap or resistance check • 2. Remove and replace the sensor at its mounting boss (exhaust pipe for NOx/O2/NH3 sensors, DEF tank for a quality sensor), torquing/sealing per spec - these are heated, CAN-networked smart sensors; aftermarket HD units commonly run $300-700 • 3. fix_title: Check NOx sensor, downstream of SCR calibration/learned values with a service tool

fix_title: Inspect and clean the accelerator pedal position sensor connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the sensor connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion, bent terminals or oil/coolant intrusion • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test the accelerator pedal position sensor signal and supply circuits
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe signal, ground and supply-voltage pins at the ECU connector • 2. Check for opens, shorts and correct reference voltage • 3. Repair chafed wiring or corroded splices, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the accelerator pedal position sensor
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify sensor air-gap or mounting per OEM spec • 2. Remove and replace the sensor and O-ring/seal • 3. Set the correct gap or torque, clear codes and verify signal quality on a scan tool

fix_title: Check the sensed target (gear teeth, reluctor ring, linkage) for damage
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Inspect the reluctor wheel, gear teeth or mechanical linkage the sensor reads for damage, debris or wear • 2. Repair or replace the damaged component • 3. Reinstall the sensor, clear codes and verify

fix_title: Check ECU power, ground and case-connector integrity
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, inspect the main ECU harness connectors for corrosion, bent pins or moisture intrusion • 2. Check the ECU's power and ground straps for a clean, tight connection • 3. Reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Test ECU supply and ground circuit wiring for the affected channel
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Verify battery voltage reaches the ECU's power pins with the key on • 2. Check chassis ground points for corrosion or a poor connection • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the engine control unit (ECU) (or the affected internal module)
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the fault persists after a reflash and clean power/ground • 2. Replace the ECU/module and transfer or re-program its configuration data • 3. Clear codes and verify with a full system scan

fix_title: Reflash/reprogram the engine control unit (ECU) with the latest calibration
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Connect the OEM diagnostic tool and check for a newer software/calibration release • 2. Reflash the ECU per the OEM procedure • 3. Clear codes, run a full DTC scan and road-test

fix_title: Replace the EGR valve actuator
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the EGR valve actuator assembly and its gasket/clamp • 2. Install the replacement, torque fasteners per spec and reconnect the harness • 3. Clear codes, run the actuator's self-calibration/learn procedure if the OEM tool supports one, and confirm normal operation

fix_title: Inspect and clean the EGR valve actuator connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the EGR valve actuator • 2. Check pins for corrosion and the harness for chafing or heat damage near the exhaust • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes and cycle the actuator with a service tool

fix_title: Test the EGR valve actuator motor/coil circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the motor or coil circuit at the connector • 2. Check winding resistance against spec and continuity/insulation to ground • 3. Repair chafed or shorted wiring, clear codes and re-test with a commanded sweep

fix_title: Free up and clean a sticking EGR valve actuator
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Remove the EGR valve actuator (or access it in place per OEM procedure) • 2. Clean carbon and soot buildup from the bore/shaft with an approved solvent, working the shaft through its full travel • 3. Reinstall, clear codes and command a full-range sweep with a service tool to confirm smooth travel

fix_title: Test the dashboard warning lamp or indicator output driver circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Back-probe the output pin at the ECU/module connector • 2. Check for a short to ground/battery or an open in the wiring to the lamp/indicator • 3. Repair as needed, clear codes

fix_title: Inspect and clean the dashboard warning lamp or indicator connector
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Key off, unplug the lamp/indicator connector • 2. Check pins for corrosion or a loose crimp • 3. Apply dielectric grease, reseat, clear codes

fix_title: Replace the failed bulb, LED module or indicator
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Confirm the bulb/LED itself is not simply burned out • 2. Replace the bulb or indicator module • 3. Clear codes and verify the indicator responds to a commanded test

fix_title: Repair chafed or corroded wiring on this circuit
step_by_step_instructions: 1. Repair chafed or corroded wiring, clear codes
procedure_rationale: Done only when the circuit test finds damaged wiring. The parts cost is carried from the original test-and-repair step, whose time covered both halves and is not carried.

fix_title: Reconfigure the aftermarket device's address per its installation manual
step_by_step_instructions: 1. When disconnecting the device cleared the conflict, set its source address as its installation manual directs, then reconnect it
procedure_rationale: Split from the aftermarket-device check because reconfiguring the device is conditional: it is done only when disconnecting the device clears the conflict. Changing a device setting buys nothing, so no parts apply, and the original time covered the check and the reconfiguration together, so it is not carried.
